Pursuant to State and County Directives, the physical access to the meeting has been suspended. To
provide members of the public access to the meeting and an opportunity to comment on items on this the
Agenda, the following opportunity has been established:

Public Comments

Please email all public comments to CScommission@sgch.org and include the following on the subject line
of your email: the section (Public Comment, Consent, Public Hearing, Continued Business, New Business)
and Item Number you are commenting on. The Staff will read public comments into the record for up to
the three-minute limit. Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read.
Example: PUBLIC COMMENT: New Business Item A
Watch the Meeting Online

https://www.youtube.com/CityofSanGabriel

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  FEBRUARY 7, 2022
   City of San Gabriel
  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  March 7, 2022

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Community Services Department Staff

BY:  Christina Alatorre, Recreation Supervisor

SUBJECT:  Monthly Department Report

Aquatics
Smith Park Pool continues normal winter operations with public lap swim offerings and
user group pool use. Spring swim lessons are now being offered on Saturdays from April
30 through May 28. Registration is available online and in-person through the Community
Services Department.

The aquatics division is seeking Lifeguard candidates for spring and summer swim aquatic
program offerings. In an effort to recruit additional aquatics staff, the Community Services
Department offered an American Red Cross Lifeguard Certification course on February
19-20. Seven participants have successfully passed the course. An additional course will
be offered April 23-24. Those interested in applying to be a Lifeguard can apply at
www.sangabrielcity.com/181/Job-Opportunities.

Contract Classes
Classes for the Spring session will begin the week of March 28. Registration for these
classes began on March 1.

Effective July 1, 2022, the City implemented a 2.9% credit card authorization fee on all
credit card transactions. The department has been enforcing the fee on the picnic rentals,
facility rentals and passport transactions since that time. After determining the best
implementation option for customers and staff the 2.9% fee will now be added to the cost
of classes and trips as well.

Facilities and Picnic Rentals
Staff are evaluating the needs of the Adult Recreation Center to determine projects that
are best suited for immediate attention and those that are most appropriate for future

  4-B
 fiscal years. These projects include new windows, painting and flooring. In addition, some
of the equipment is in need of repair or replacement such as the tables and chairs.
Evaluating and executing these projects will allow staff to continue to offer the space for
private rentals, community group meetings and events, and older adult programing.

Kennedy Baseball Field has four current user groups renting the field for baseball
practices. The Public Works Department continue to do a great job to maintain and
prepare the field for regular use.

Older Adult Programs and Trips
The trip to the BAPS Temple in Chino Hills is scheduled for March 26. As of March 2,
2022 there are 14 people registered. The day will start with a tour of the Temple and the
surrounding grounds followed by lunch on site. It is sure to be a beautiful day filled with
cultural enlightenment. Staff will be scheduling one trip per month with a primary focus
of staying within the Prop A funded region. This will enable to cost to the participant to
remain low. To submit a trip idea or request please email Matthew Morales-Stevens,
Recreation Supervisor at mmoralesstevens@sgch.org.

In partnership with the YWCA of the San Gabriel Valley the Department continues to
provide free meals to seniors within the City of San Gabriel. It has successfully
transitioned to an in-person pick-up at the Adult Recreation Center. Participants that are
unable to pick-up in person are transferred to the delivery program directly through the
YWCA. The city is currently serving 159 older adults. Safety precautions are still in place
such as masks, social distancing and sanitizing.

Youth Programs
After School Program - The after school program continues at Coolidge, McKinley,
Washington and Wilson Elementary Schools. Each school site celebrated Lunar New Year,
year of the tiger, by participating the Lunar New Year Art Competition. Each participant
was given an opportunity to create an art poster celebrating Lunar New Year. Community
Services staff selected their top art pieces per age category. The top three winners in each
age category were given a certificate and ribbon, with their artwork showcased on the
Community Services Department webpage.

In honor of Black History month, staff have included various themed activities throughout
school sites. Washington and Wilson Elementary Schools have offered an “I have a dream”
art activity based off of Dr. Martin Luther King that incorporates each participants dreams

  4-B
 for the future. Coolidge Elementary participants shared inspirational quotes made by
important people in history. McKinley Elementary implemented chalk art showcasing
unity, important figures and the significance of celebrating black history.

Jefferson Middle School - The Jefferson Middle School sports program incorporated
Black History into their sports program curriculum by showcasing iconic sports figures
and their contributions to their communities.

Basketball Clinics at Jefferson Middle School are currently running and will come to a close
on March 11. Staff are preparing participants for an upcoming Basketball Skills Challenge
hosted by Southern California Municipal Athletic Federation (SCMAF). Players have
competed in an internal competition to determine the six players who will represent the
city in the Skills Challenge on March 19 in the City of Walnut. This is a great opportunity
for our youth to showcase their skills, build confidence in their game, and compete against
players in surrounding cities.

Special Events
Health and Wellness Fair – The Health and Wellness Fair will take place on Sunday,
March 27 from 10:00 am to 2:00 pm at the Adult Recreation Center. The Community
Services Department is partnering with the USC School of Pharmacy to offer free class
demonstrations, medication review, and educational booths. There will also be free
screenings available including blood pressure, blood glucose, body fat analysis &
osteoporosis.

Spring Celebration - The 77th Annual Spring Celebration will take place on Saturday, April
16 from 7: 00 am to 11:00 am. The City is partnering with the Kiwanis Club of San Gabriel.
The primary components include a pancake breakfast and egg hunt. In addition,
participants will be able to enjoy pancake races, a DJ, crafts, and photos with Mr. Bunny.
